conclusion: The reported Room N values are analyzer-derived parent-key groups, not verified static RoomId counts. The data supports grouping/classification mismatch as a plausible contributor to the 7-versus-11/10 discrepancy, but does not determine whether generator semantics also contribute.

model_observations.grouping_unit: Captured scene instances are grouped by parent_key and labeled Room N; these labels are not proven static RoomId values.
model_observations.classification: The CARGO run has ROOM_DEADEND-named paths in five groups (indices 3, 4, 5, 6, 9) but all 11 groups are classified main. The newer MEDI run has such paths in three groups (indices 1, 3, 7) while all 10 groups are classified main. A dead-end-named prefab path therefore does not by itself identify a generated dead-end room.
model_observations.inference: The inspected analyzer code directly explains why scene basenames containing ROOM_DEADEND can remain inside main_room parent groups: classification uses a family-level DEADEND_* test and group-size rule. It also establishes that Room N counts parent_key groups, not static IDs. It does not resolve whether 11 groups arise from generator branches, grouping granularity, or a different interpretation of the Rooms parameter.
